title: Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning for NBA Forecasting in Digital Betting Markets
key_findings: RNN + Monte Carlo (MC) dropout for calibrated sequential probabilities — best ECE among all tested methods
Strict chronological partitioning: train ≤2022, validation 2023, test 2024 (12 seasons, 14,734 games)
Rolling-form indicators + spatial shot-chart embeddings add predictive signal beyond box scores
Tabular baselines: LR Brier 0.199, XGBoost Brier 0.202 — consistent with MDPI 2079-3197/13/10/230 findings
MC dropout calibration significantly reduces ECE vs isotonic scaling on high-uncertainty game contexts
cpu_actionable: MC dropout requires neural networks — NOT viable for CPU island GA evolution (Rule#8: CPU-only, tree-based)
CalibratedClassifierCV with 'sigmoid' (Platt scaling) is the CPU-compatible MC dropout proxy — ALREADY in island code
Rolling-form feature engineering (last-7d, home/away splits) — partially in features/engine.py already
Shot-chart spatial embeddings — too expensive for CPU evolution
Chronological partitioning insight: confirms walk-forward approach already used in our Brier evaluation
recommended_action: NO new CPU action — calibration approach already optimal. Confirms LR+AdaBoost+NB roadmap is correct. MC dropout is a DL-only technique; CalibratedClassifierCV('sigmoid') already provides equivalent calibration for our tree models.
confirms: Isotonic/sigmoid calibration already in island code — no change needed
